sections.title: Conversion of Infinitives (to + V1 → to be + V3)
sections.content:
When a sentence contains an infinitive (to + V1), convert it into passive form using 'to be + V3'.
Example: She wants to complete the project.
Step 1: Identify the infinitive phrase (to complete the project).
Step 2: Identify the object (the project).
Step 3: Change 'to complete' into 'to be completed'.
Step 4: Place the object before the infinitive phrase.
Step 5: Reconstruct the sentence without changing the main verb tense.
Answer: She wants the project to be completed.

sections.title: Conversion of Gerunds (-ing → being + V3)
sections.content:
When a gerund (-ing form) acts on an object, convert it into 'being + V3' in passive.
Example: I remember people praising her.
Step 1: Identify the gerund (praising).
Step 2: Identify the object (her).
Step 3: Change 'praising' to 'being praised'.
Step 4: Change pronoun if needed (her → she/her possessive form).
Step 5: Rewrite the sentence logically.
Answer: I remember her being praised.

sections.title: Sentences Starting with 'It is time to...'
sections.content:
Structure: It is time to + V1
Passive form: It is time for + object + to be + V3
Example: It is time to announce the results.
Step 1: Identify the object (the results).
Step 2: Change 'to announce' to 'to be announced'.
Step 3: Add 'for + object' after 'time'.
Step 4: Maintain original tense.
Step 5: Form the correct sentence.
Answer: It is time for the results to be announced.

sections.title: Sentences with 'There is/are...'
sections.content:
Structure: There is/are + object + to + V1
Passive form: There is/are + object + to be + V3
Example: There are many issues to resolve.
Step 1: Identify infinitive (to resolve).
Step 2: Convert to 'to be resolved'.
Step 3: Keep 'There are' unchanged.
Step 4: Maintain number agreement.
Step 5: Rewrite the sentence.
Answer: There are many issues to be resolved.

sections.title: Hidden Agents (Implied Doer)
sections.content:
Sometimes the doer is not mentioned in passive voice.
Example: The thief was arrested.
Step 1: Identify passive structure (was + V3).
Step 2: Ask who performed the action (context clue: police).
Step 3: Make the hidden agent the subject.
Step 4: Convert verb into correct active tense.
Step 5: Rewrite sentence logically.
Answer: The police arrested the thief.

sections.title: Passive of Causative Verbs (Make, Have, Get)
sections.content:
1. Make
Example: He made me cry.
Step 1: Identify object (me).
Step 2: Convert 'made' into 'was made'.
Step 3: Add 'to' before base verb (cry → to cry).
Step 4: Change pronoun (me → I).
Step 5: Add agent if required.
Answer: I was made to cry by him.

2. Have/Get
Example: I had him repair my car.
Step 1: Identify real object (my car).
Step 2: Convert into passive causative structure.
Step 3: Use 'had/get + object + V3'.
Step 4: Remove unnecessary agent.
Step 5: Form final sentence.
Answer: I had my car repaired.

sections.title: Quasipassive Verbs
sections.content:
Some active verbs have passive meaning.
Example: Sugar tastes sweet.
Step 1: Identify that 'tastes' shows quality, not action by subject.
Step 2: Understand implied passive meaning (when it is tasted).
Step 3: Expand sentence logically.
Step 4: Add 'when it is + V3'.
Step 5: Maintain clarity.
Answer: Sugar is sweet when it is tasted.

sections.title: Important Rules
sections.content:
1. Infinitive → to be + V3.
2. Gerund → being + V3.
3. In 'make', add 'to' in passive form.
4. Identify hidden agents carefully.
5. Do not disturb original tense or logical meaning.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 focuses on complex transformations such as infinitives, gerunds, causatives, hidden agents, and quasipassive verbs. Always identify the object first, preserve tense, apply correct passive structure, and maintain logical clarity.

tricks.title: Infinitive Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Whenever you see 'to + V1', change it to 'to be + V3' in passive.

tricks.title: Make Rule
tricks.explanation: 'Make + object + V1' becomes 'object + was made to + V1'.
tricks.example: He made me laugh → I was made to laugh.

tricks.title: Hidden Agent Rule
tricks.explanation: If no agent is given, infer logically (police, people, someone).
tricks.example: The law was passed → The government passed the law.

tricks.title: There Structure Trick
tricks.explanation: 'to + V1' after There is/are becomes 'to be + V3'.

tricks.title: Quasipassive Clue
tricks.explanation: If subject shows quality, expand using 'when it is + V3'.
tricks.example: The book sells well → The book is sold well.
